context: Field theory: monic irreducible polynomial of an algebraic element

formulations.text: If an element alpha of an extension E/k is algebraic over k, its minimal polynomial over k is the unique monic polynomial generating the kernel of evaluation k[t] to E at alpha; it is irreducible over k.
formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.

context: Field theory: minimal root-containing extension of a polynomial

formulations.text: For a nonconstant polynomial P over a field F, a splitting field is a field extension E/F in which P factors into linear terms and which is generated over F by all its roots.
formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.

context: Topology: descending chain condition on closed subsets

formulations.text: A topological space is Noetherian when every descending sequence of its closed subsets eventually becomes constant.
formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.

formulations.text: A topological space X is quasi-compact if each open cover of X contains a finite subcollection that still covers X; no Hausdorff condition is required.
formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.

context: Topology: inverse images of quasi-compact open sets

formulations.text: A continuous map f:X to Y is quasi-compact if the inverse image of each quasi-compact open subset of Y is quasi-compact in X.
formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.

context: Commutative algebra: Zariski topology on prime ideals

formulations.text: For a commutative ring R, the prime spectrum Spec(R) is the set consisting of all prime ideals of R, equipped with the Zariski topology whose closed sets comprise the common zero-locus sets V(I).
formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.

context: Category theory: simultaneous left and right exactness

formulations.text: A functor between categories with the requisite finite limits and colimits is exact if it preserves both finite limits and finite colimits (equivalently it is both left exact and right exact).
formulations.editorial_note: Source-checked mathematical candidate; no independent human verification claimed.

formulations.text: A field extension E/F has degree equal to the vector-space dimension of E over F; the extension is finite exactly when this dimension is a finite integer.
